author: Mark Atwood
text: REVERSAL 2026-05-12 (Mark, interactive, second pass): closing again with the OPPOSITE decision -- C) Skip, no pkix-policy-oscal crate. Yesterday's A (file new crate) was made on discoverability-via-crate-name grounds, which assumed OSCAL Profile JSON has substantive policy-DSL value. Re-examination today asked the underlying question: can OSCAL make decisions? Answer: NO. OSCAL is a compliance-document vocabulary that DESCRIBES controls and SELECTS from catalogs; it does not carry predicate logic. The validator's substantive decisions live in Rust Lint impls. OSCAL Profile JSON is functionally equivalent to a TOML/YAML config file listing Lint IDs to enable + parameters. This is the same observation Mark made in the 2026-05-11 OSCAL demotion ('compliance-document vocabulary, not rule-predicate DSL'); it applies here too. Under that lens, shipping pkix-policy-oscal would be 'we ship a fancy-named adapter for a config format that has equivalent semantic value to TOML'. Discoverability argument doesn't outweigh that. CONSUMERS WHO WANT OSCAL Profile JSON support have everything they need: Lint::id() public API, LintRunner public constructor, pkix-lint OSCAL parsing types (already public behind 'oscal' feature flag from PKIX-9vnx). About 50 lines of serde_json + filter + LintRunner::new. WORKSPACE'S OSCAL STORY post-reversal: emit-only. pkix-lint/src/oscal/* continues to emit Assessment Results in OSCAL format for compliance reporting (real value, already shipped). Workspace does NOT consume OSCAL Profile JSON for config. Asymmetry is intentional and reflects the actual value asymmetry: emit-for-compliance-reporting is genuinely useful; consume-for-config is bounded. CASCADES: PKIX-jy95.9 (impl epic filed yesterday) closes WONTFIX with same rationale. AGENTS.md inventory removes pkix-policy-oscal. Memory pkix-jy95-5-oscal-crate-2026-05-12 superseded by pkix-jy95-5-skip-oscal-2026-05-12.
